strategy.summary: Pure-Python sympy geometry bug: Triangle.excenters in sympy/geometry/polygon.py has missing parentheses in exc_coords and wrong side-length assignment. Reproduce by checking out the buggy commit 3b255faf11bc from source (no build), applying the PR's test diff, and running the two affected tests in test_polygon.py. The transition is test_excenters and the modified test_polygon assertion failing on the buggy tree and passing on the fixed tree. The environment is unbounded because no sympy version is documented, so the strategy pins the buggy commit itself.

pinned_because: sympy is unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era ceiling), so the source tree at the buggy commit 3b255faf11bc is used as the sympy version instead of a pip release
mpmath is a runtime dependency of sympy and is left unpinned because no constraint was stated
pytest is used only as the runner; the sympy source is run from the repo root so the local tree shadows any installed sympy

strategy.test_command: git checkout 3b255faf11bc && git apply reproducing_test.patch && python -m pytest sympy/geometry/tests/test_polygon.py::test_excenters sympy/geometry/tests/test_polygon.py::test_polygon -q
strategy.reproducing_test: sympy/geometry/tests/test_polygon.py: new test_excenters (t=Triangle(Point(0,0),Point(6,0),Point(0,2)); asserts t.excenters[t.sides[0]]==Point(sqrt(10)+4,sqrt(10)+4), t.excenters[t.sides[1]]==Point(2-sqrt(10),-2+sqrt(10)), t.excenters[t.sides[2]]==Point(2+sqrt(10),-sqrt(10)-2)) plus the changed test_polygon assertion t1.excenters[t1.sides[2]]==Point2D(5*sqrt(2)/2,-5*sqrt(2)/2) (previously 25*sqrt(2)).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 3b255faf11bc with the test diff applied, test_excenters fails with AssertionError on its first assert (buggy value Point2D(12*sqrt(10), 2/3 + sqrt(10)/3) != Point(sqrt(10)+4, sqrt(10)+4)), and test_polygon fails at the excenter assertion for t1.sides[2]. On the fixed revision with the same diff, both tests pass with exact symbolic equality. The transition is fail to pass for both tests.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "from sympy import *; from sympy.geometry import Point, Triangle; t=Triangle(Point(0,0),Point(6,0),Point(0,2)); print(t.excenters[t.sides[0]])"  (run from repo root so the local tree is imported; buggy prints 12*sqrt(10) form, fixed prints sqrt(10)+4 form)
risks: The tree must be the buggy commit 3b255faf11bc: the test diff is written against the pre-fix test_polygon.py, so applying it to a later tree will fail for unrelated reasons or not apply cleanly.

Exact equality of symbolic sqrt expressions depends on sympy's simplification at that commit; running against a newer pip sympy could change canonical forms, so the git checkout must be used rather than pip install sympy.
The expected values are asserted in the tests and docstring; the correct formula is only linked (GeeksforGeeks), not reproduced, so the reference is the test assertions themselves.

No platform, architecture, sanitiser, or threading dependence is stated in the evidence; the defect is a pure arithmetic/precedence error, so it should appear on any platform, but this is inferred rather than documented.
bin/test and ./setup.py test are listed in the README, but -k selection of a single test is not guaranteed by bin/test at this era, so pytest node IDs are used instead; pytest must be installed.
The PR also updated the docstring example; doctests are not part of the transition and are not planned for.

oracle.reference_source: sympy/geometry/tests/test_polygon.py assertions added or changed by the PR (test_excenters and t1.sides[2] excenter check)
oracle.why: Excenters are symbolic sympy expressions involving sqrt, so the tests use exact == comparison rather than a float tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy tree, the first assertion in test_excenters compares t.excenters[t.sides[0]] (buggy Point2D(12*sqrt(10), 2/3 + sqrt(10)/3)) with Point(sqrt(10)+4, sqrt(10)+4); the symbolic equality is False, so AssertionError is raised. The altered test_polygon assertion also fails because the buggy value for t1.sides[2] is Point2D(25*sqrt(2), -5*sqrt(2)/2), not the expected Point2D(5*sqrt(2)/2, -5*sqrt(2)/2).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed tree with the same test diff, the parenthesized exc_coords and corrected a,b,c = s[1].length, s[2].length, s[0].length give sqrt(10)+4 etc., so all asserts in test_excenters and the t1.sides[2] check in test_polygon evaluate to True and both tests pass.
